headline: Oceans contain most of Earth's living space—an alien world teeming with life we're only beginning to understand
universal_truth: What we don't see can be vast; the invisible world may be larger than the visible
fun_facts: Oceans cover 71% of Earth's surface and contain 99% of the living space on the planet
More than 80% of the ocean remains unexplored and unmapped
The deepest ocean trenches are home to life—creatures thriving in crushing pressure and total darkness
discussion_questions: Why do we know more about the moon's surface than the ocean floor?
What might live in the unexplored 80% of the ocean?
How does ocean life differ from land life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We call this planet 'Earth,' but it should be called 'Ocean.' Water covers 71% of the surface and contains 99% of the living space. Below the waves is an alien world—dark, deep, and full of life we're only beginning to discover.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We've mapped distant planets, but over 80% of our own ocean remains unexplored. What lives in the deep ocean, and why has it been so hard to discover?
cliff.prompt: Why is ocean life so mysterious?

options.text: Extreme pressure, darkness, and vastness make deep ocean exploration extremely difficult
options.response: Yes. The deep ocean is hostile to humans and our technology. Pressure crushes, darkness blinds, and the sheer volume is overwhelming. It's Earth's last frontier.

options.text: We've focused on land and space exploration instead
options.response: Priorities matter, but the technical challenges of the deep ocean are immense...

q1.title: Vast Volume
q1.script: The ocean contains 321 million cubic miles of water. If you flattened Earth's surface, the ocean would cover the whole planet 2 miles deep. This volume provides 99% of Earth's living space. Land is a thin skin on an ocean world.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Vast Volume"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Deep Life
q2.script: Even in the deepest trenches—7 miles down, in crushing pressure and total darkness—life thrives. Creatures we've never imagined, feeding on chemicals from underwater vents or falling debris from above. Life adapts to every condition.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Unknown Majority
q3.script: We've mapped Mars better than our own ocean floor. Over 80% of the ocean is unexplored. Thousands, maybe millions of species await discovery. The greatest unexplored territory isn't in space—it's underwater.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What we don't see can be vast. The ocean teaches that the invisible world may be larger than the visible. Mystery surrounds us, hidden beneath the surface, waiting to be explored.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 139. Tomorrow, we'll explore animals like us—mammals. Until then, consider that most of life on Earth lives in a world you've never seen.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Ocean Perspective - Appreciate the Unseen
growTrack.activity: Look at a map or globe and notice how much is blue. 71% of the planet, 99% of the living space, 80% unexplored. What creatures might be swimming in the deep right now, never seen by human eyes? The mystery is real and immense.
